sentences.text: Eoenantiornis is recognized as one of the earliest known derived members of the enantiornithine bird lineage.
The specific holotype specimen, which serves as the primary reference for the species, belonged to an individual that had not yet reached full maturity.
The species Eoenantiornis buhleri was first named and described in 1999 by Hou Lianhu, Larry Martin, Zhou Zhonghe, and John Alan Feduccia.
This fossil was uncovered at Heitizigou in Liaoning, located within the lower Yixian Formation.
A complete redescription of the genus occurred in 2005 to update its scientific understanding.
Originally, the organism was assigned to the family Eoenantiornithidae and the order Eoenantiornithiformes.
However, in 2005, these original classifications were discarded, and the species was instead placed within the clade Euenantiornithes.
Current taxonomic systems place the superorder classification for Eoenantiornis as Euenantiornithes.
The family classification remains listed as Eoenantiornithidae in some contexts.
This extinct genus lived during the early Cretaceous period, approximately 124.6 million years ago.
It inhabited the region now known as Asia at the beginning of the Cretaceous, specifically during the Aptian age around 122.46 million years ago.
The estimated time range for Eoenantiornis spans from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
